newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss franc ends sharply lower, SNB remarks push.
newsitem.headline: Swiss franc ends sharply lower, SNB remarks push.

text.p: 1545 GMT - The Swiss franc ended sharply easier against the dollar and mark, pushed down by remarks from Swiss National Bank (SNB) officials that underscored the Swiss central bank's determination to keep the franc from rising.
"Today's remarks helped pull down the franc. No one dares go long of francs right now," said one dealer.
Medium-term, the market sees further franc easing.
The dollar was also helped by robust U.S. consumer confidence data, which renewed speculation about higher rates.

Among today's remarks by SNB chairman Hans Meyer in Zurich was that the SNB would take steps to protect the Swiss recovery and that he was not "entirely happy" with the recent strengthening of the franc.

In Geneva SNB vice-chairman Jean-Pierre Roth said the SNB would continue to inject liquidity into the money market to ease upward pressure on the Swiss franc. * Dollar ends at 1.4156/4166 francs vs this morning's 1.4035/4045 and yesterday's closer of 1.4007/4012. * Mark ends at 83.40/41 centimes vs yesterday's 82.94/97
